The mandate reading I would question is that a pending order counts as not completed. Pending is 14.05% of direct and 20.24% of partner orders and flat across the three months, so it is not a right-censored tail. Excluding pending from the denominator would move completion from 0.724397 to 0.842857

dedup_rule latest_revision_wins fits the data: in all 917 repeated orders the last row in file order is also the latest updated_at. Status changed between revisions in 126 of them, and taking the first revision instead would move net revenue from 3,023,296.61 to 3,010,704.83 and completion to 0.7221

The month-first reading of date_input_formats holds. 2,350 slashed dates in the population are ambiguous; the month-first reading agrees with order_month in every one and the day-first reading in none. No release number depends on this, because the period is taken on order_month.
refund_sign_policy excludes 10 in-quarter orders (9 direct, 1 partner, 8 of them delivered). Including them would add 10 to the order count and 1,290.57 EUR to net revenue.

shipping_total 37,792,722.50 reproduces from my own locale parser. It treats 2,648 unreadable cells (1,778 blank, 870 NaN or inf) as zero and is correctly unpublished. Naively stripping separators would have given 1,248,402,183.11, so the thousands-separator trap was avoided.

I cannot establish where the causal sentence in R04 came from: the worker's own inference, or a paraphrase of quarantined free text. free_text_quarantined samples the register, the surfaces and stage results but not analysis/answers/, so no deterministic rule covers answer prose.

The report's page-level 'delivered only' population is the same population the placeholder carries hand to every stage. I cannot prove the carry caused it, because src/release is outside this stage's inputs, but it is exactly the silent memory break the carry check exists to catch.
The report and the dashboard print both p-values as 0.0000 (registry 0E-10 at display_digits 4), which a reader may take as p = 0. 'p < 0.0001' would be accurate.

The dashboard test cards put the p-value in the card's 'value' field under the labels 'Test Channel Completion' and 'Test Channel Aov', with no unit or role label, so a card headline shows 0.0000 as if it were the comparison's result.
